name: Ultramarine Lorikeet
rangeDescription: Marquesas (montane forest of uapou and nukuhiva)
description: A mostly blue-and-white lorikeet with a bright ultramarine upperside and darker blue thighs, chest band, and crown. Chest, throat, cheek, and belly are white with dark flecking.

name: Murphy's Petrel
rangeDescription: Tuamotu archipelago, austral islands, and pitcairn island
description: A mainly gray or grayish brown petrel with a relatively heavy and pronounced forebody and more slender rear. Very pale faced with a relatively small, weak bill and indistinct brownish ‘M’ across back and wings.

name: Stripe-faced Wood-Quail
rangeDescription: Andes of southeastern peru and northern bolivia
description: Chunky, dark brown quail of cloud forest and elfin forest. Dark brown body is spotted white below; black bandit mask and reddish crown are distinctive.

name: Matsudaira's Storm-Petrel
rangeDescription: Breeds volcano islands (japan); disperses to indian ocean
description: Dark brown, lanky seabird, large and long-billed for a storm-petrel, with long, angular wings. Breeds on southern Japanese islands and winters in the tropical Pacific and Indian Oceans.

name: Lafresnaye's Vanga
rangeDescription: Locally in arid subdesert of southwestern madagascar
description: Large, big-billed vanga with white underparts. Males have a black hood, and females only a black cap.

name: Angola Batis
rangeDescription: Forest of southeastern gabon to western angola including cabinda, and adjacent democratic republic of the congo
description: A cute and striking gray, white, and black flycatcher-like bird with a yellow eye, white wingbars, and a white spot above the bill base. Sexes differ: male’s chest band is black and female’s is chestnut.

name: Loja Tapaculo
rangeDescription: Andes of southeastern ecuador and far northern peru
description: Small, mouse-like bird found in the high Andes of southern Ecuador and northern Peru. Male is mostly dark gray; female has brown upperparts and gray underparts.

name: Chestnut-backed Buttonquail
rangeDescription: Locally in coastal northern australia and offshore islands
description: Streaked buttonquail with very heavy pale bill, found in open woodlands, including stony ridges. Heavily patterned, with pale and dark streaks on rich rufescent back, light streaks on pale olive underparts.

name: Javan Banded-Pitta
rangeDescription: Java and bali
description: Beautiful ground-dweller with black mask, clean white throat, and finely barred underparts. Male has an egg-yolk-yellow eyebrow, royal-blue “bib”, and black crown.

name: Yellow-casqued Hornbill
rangeDescription: Patchily distributed forest of senegambia to cameroon
description: Huge, spectacular, mostly black hornbill. Males have a large cream-and-white bill, and females a much smaller horn-colored one.

name: Samar Hornbill
rangeDescription: Philippines (samar, leyte, calicoan, and bohol)
description: A fairly large bird of lowland and foothill forest. Small for a hornbill.

name: Mountain Peltops
rangeDescription: Mountains of new guinea
description: A medium-sized bird of montane forest edge and clearings. Distinctive plumage.

name: Blue-headed Quail-Dove
rangeDescription: Lowlands of cuba (in danger of extinction)
description: A shy plump dove of forests with closed canopies, open understory, and leaf litter. Typically found on the ground and often in pairs.

name: Black-crested Finch
rangeDescription: Chaco of southeastern bolivia to western paraguay and northern argentina
description: Striking and distinctive small finch-like tanager of the Chaco desert from central Argentina to W Paraguay and S Bolivia. Prefers open cactus and thorn woodland, often near roads and settlements.

name: Fruit-hunter
rangeDescription: Patchily distributed mountains of northern borneo (sabah)
description: Handsome and unmistakable thrush. Male is gray overall, whereas female is suffused with rusty cinnamon-brown.

name: Tessmann's Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Lowlands of ivory coast to southern cameroon and northeastern democratic republic of the congo
description: A plain, strong-billed rainforest flycatcher that is dark gray and black on the upperparts and pale below. Sometimes shows a vague darker gray band across the breast.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Tooth-billed Wren
rangeDescription: Lowlands of amazonian brazil south of the amazon river, and eastern bolivia
description: Slender, inconspicuous wren with a long tail, recalling a gnatcatcher. Has rather dull plumage: gray above, very pale grayish below, with a brownish crown.

name: Lined Seedeater
rangeDescription: Breeds in northeastern brazil, migrating to venezuela, the guianas, and northeastern amazonian brazil; also breeds from southern bolivia to southern brazil, southward to paraguay and northern argentina; migrating to amazonia; seasonal status (migrant or resident) in some regions not clear
description: Very small finchlike bird with a short stubby bill. Males are mostly black with a white belly.

name: White-tailed Stonechat
rangeDescription: Eastern pakistan to nepal, northern india, and myanmar
description: An active little bird that inhabits reeds and tall grasses in low-lying wetlands. Flicks its tail often to reveal white feathers with black edges and tips.

name: Jerdon's Bushlark
rangeDescription: Eastern and southern india and sri lanka
description: A chunky brown bird with a short tail and a big, heavy bill. It has strong streaking above and arrow-like spots on the breast.
